# Dryer Notes

## Overview

A vented drum unit that has served me four years without a repair. It handles three loads of clothes back to back on a warm setting, and the run time for a full drum sits around fifty minutes. I keep the manual and the receipt in the folder with the other appliance paperwork. The drum is a 7 kg size, which is plenty for the two of us and the occasional guest. It sits in the utility corner on a rubber mat so it does not walk on the tiles during a spin.

## Troubleshooting

If a load comes out damp, the most likely cause is a clogged filter or a squashed vent hose. I check both before I blame the heating element. A long run time points at restricted airflow out to the wall vent. A drum that turns but stays cold usually means the thermal fuse has tripped. The moisture sensor strips inside the door get a wipe with vinegar when the unit begins stopping early. A high pitched squeal on start up is a worn drum roller.

## Notes

Rinse the lint filter under the tap every month, then let it air dry before sliding it back. The vent hose gets checked for kinks whenever I move the machine, and the outside flap gets cleared of nests in spring. I run an empty warm cycle once a year to clear any residue. A damp cloth keeps the cabinet clean; I never use polish on the front panel. Delicates go in a mesh bag so they do not catch on the drum ribs.
